flaws.title: Aligned starting tick can be skipped in the downward iterator, causing wrong zero-for-one liquidity accounting
flaws.sequence:
1. A pool's current tick before a top-of-block zero-for-one swap is exactly an initialized multiple of tick spacing `t`.
2. `AngstromL2.afterSwap` calls `_zeroForOneDistributeTax`, which calls `TickIteratorLib.initDown(..., startTick=t, endTick< t)`, and `initDown` calls this `reset`.
3. In `reset`, the iterator only leaves `currentTick == startTick` for one special case; otherwise it calls `_advanceToNextDown` from `startTick - 1`, so the initialized starting tick `t` is skipped.
4. `CompensationPriceFinder.getZeroForOne` and then `AngstromL2._zeroForOneCreditRewards` consume that iterator and therefore fail to apply `liquidityNet` at `t` even though the walk crossed `t`.
5. If no overlapping liquidity exists, the later subtraction at lower ticks can underflow and revert the swap; if overlapping liquidity does exist, rewards are computed with the wrong active liquidity and an attacker can arrange positions so their liquidity just below `t` captures rewards they were not owed.
flaws.impact: Zero-for-one swaps that start on an initialized boundary can revert, and in overlapping-liquidity setups rewards can be misdistributed so an attacker steals LP rewards.
flaws.known_finding: All rewards can be stolen due to incorrect active liquidity calculations when the current tick is an exact multiple of the tick spacing at the upper end of a liquidity range
